Variants.Content: Westeros has no realm-wide standing army; large-scale war relies chiefly on lords summoning bannermen, knights, squires, peasant levies, and hired men-at-arms according to oath. The size of an army depends not only on banners, but on harvests, horses, roads, supplies, the season, and whether a lord can persuade or compel his subordinates to march. Nobles regard the levy as duty and glory, while peasants see the risk of leaving their fields, losing labor, and having their families go hungry. Terms of service, quality of equipment, and degrees of loyalty vary widely, and prolonged campaigning wears down the network of bannermen.

Before levied hosts and feudal armies, lords speak of rights, clerks speak of procedure, and common folk speak of whether they can make it home safely; command and execution decide whether a written order is a binding obligation or the start of another round of bargaining.

When lords and merchants speak of levied armies, they think first of war chests, supply lines, and alliances.
